ai.description: Elliot's Forest Lizard reaches 20 cm in length. It is brown with a dark, pale-edged patch behind the tympanum and a distinct, elongated nuchal crest. Males display a bright yellow or orange throat fan.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Monilesaurus ellioti* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, white or cream-colored stripe running along its upper lip, contrasting with its dark head.
ai.habitat: Elliot's Forest Lizard inhabits the rainforests and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Elliot's Forest Lizard is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on tree trunks or rocks before actively foraging for small insects among the forest undergrowth.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Monilesaurus ellioti* is oviparous, laying clutches of 2–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months, from March to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Monilesaurus ellioti* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring across the states of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka at elevations between 600 and 1,800 meters.
